Summary

As an organization user, I want to sign in to eCore Command Center using my organization credentials so that I can access the application

Story

As an organization user of eCore Command Center
I want to sign in using my organization credentials
So that I can access the application with my assigned permissions

Context

The eCore Command Center login page is the entry point to the application. It
supports more than one kind of sign-in, and the user tells the system which kind
they are using before entering their details. Organization users authenticate
against their organization rather than against an individual business entity, so
the organization they belong to forms part of what they supply at sign-in.

The other supported sign-in kind is Business Entity Login. It exists on the same
page and the user must be able to tell the two apart and choose between them, but
its own behaviour is handled elsewhere and is not part of this story.

Which details the page asks for depends on the choice the user makes. The page is
expected to respond to that choice rather than present every possible field at
once.

What the user does

A user arrives at the login page, indicates that they are signing in on behalf of
their organization, supplies who they are, which organization they belong to, and
the secret that proves it, and submits. If everything they supplied is correct,
they arrive at the eCore Command Center Home page and can work in the application
within the limits of their organization and permissions.

Passwords are secrets and are treated as such on screen.

Not everything a user submits will be correct. Details can be wrong, and details
can be left out altogether. In neither case should the user get into the
application, and in neither case should they be left guessing about what happened.
Wrong details and missing details are different problems and the user should be
able to tell which one they have hit.

Out of Scope

Business Entity Login behaviour; Forgot Password; password reset; user creation;
organization creation; role and permission configuration; MFA and SSO; session
timeout; account lockout; exact error-message wording.

comments.body:
Continued development of the POC automation framework and completed the end-to-end framework implementation.

Finalized the workflow covering Jira requirement input, acceptance criteria generation, test plan creation, test script generation, human approval gates, test execution, and report generation.

Completed the framework setup and validated the overall workflow, with application-based execution to be continued as required.

Continued enhancing the POC automation framework based on the feedback and suggestions provided by Mustafa during the initial framework demo.

Updated the framework to support Jira tickets with or without predefined Acceptance Criteria.

• Initiated development of a new AI-assisted automation framework to analyze Jira tickets, including linked tickets and sub-stories, and convert the requirements into structured raw data and Acceptance Criteria.
  • The framework incorporates three human approval gates across the workflow: Acceptance Criteria Approval, Test Plan Approval, and Automation Approval.
  • Following the approval stages, the framework generates the Test Plan, creates BDD-based automation scripts, and executes the test scripts as part of the end-to-end automation workflow.
  • Received feedback and improvement suggestions from Mustafa and Abhinav and are currently working on incorporating the identified changes and enhancements into the framework.

• Completed the implementation of the AI-assisted automation framework and integrated v8-to-istanbul for test coverage tracking.
  • Incorporated the coverage functionality into the existing framework while ensuring that the previously implemented features and workflows continue to work without disruption, along with the required updates to related references and configurations.
  • Performed validation using multiple Jira ticket scenarios, including tickets with no Acceptance Criteria, incomplete Acceptance Criteria, and complete Acceptance Criteria, to verify the framework’s behavior across different requirement conditions.
  • The framework is now functionally complete and undergoing further validation and refinement based on the test results.

• As part of the ongoing framework design activity, reviewed the new requirement to leverage models available in FAB Studio.
  • Spent time gaining an understanding of FAB Agents and available models, including how they can be integrated and utilized within the existing automation framework.
  • Evaluated the potential integration approach and continued defining how FAB capabilities can be incorporated into the framework to support the overall automation workflow.

• As part of the ongoing framework development, implemented a Defect Analyzer Agent to support automated defect analysis during test execution.
  • The agent is designed to analyze failed test executions, identify potential defects, and automatically create a Jira defect within the same Jira story associated with the current execution.
  • This enhancement improves the end-to-end automation workflow by integrating test execution, defect identification, and Jira defect creation into the framework.

• Completed the development of the AI-assisted automation framework and validated the end-to-end workflow.
  • The framework can read and process Jira tickets, generate requirements, Acceptance Criteria, and Test Plans, and create the corresponding BDD automation artifacts, including feature files, step definitions, and page objects.
  • Implemented Healer Agents to identify and resolve locator-related and code-related issues encountered during test execution.
  • Successfully executed the generated test cases, with the applicable test cases passing and execution reports generated successfully.
  • Overall, the framework now supports an end-to-end flow from Jira requirement → test planning → BDD script generation → self-healing → execution → reporting.
